title: Do Halting Heads Really Save Compute in Looped Language Models?
abstract: arXiv:2610.32246v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Looped language models run each token through the same layers several times, and each run is one iteration. To save compute, an extra layer, the halting head, gives after each iteration the probability that the token stops there, so that easy tokens can stop early. Pretraining models from scratch, up to 1.3B parameters, we find two problems. First, heads trained on a mix of all iterations predict that tokens need under half the iterations, yet under the standard stopping rule tokens run almost every iteration, because this training never scores the single iteration where a token stops. Scoring every iteration instead fixes this, but in our runs it works only with a strong penalty favoring early stops. Second, savings are commonly reported as an average number of iterations per token, but when sequences are generated in batches that run until their slowest token stops, a model without a head is almost as good at that cost. translated_title: 循环语言模型中的停止头真的能节省计算吗？
translated_abstract: 循环语言模型让每个词元多次通过相同的层，每次通过称为一次迭代。为了节省计算量，模型引入一个额外的层——停止头，它在每次迭代后给出词元在此停止的概率，使简单的词元可以提前停止。我们从零开始预训练了参数量最高达13亿的模型，发现了两个问题。第一，在所有迭代的混合数据上训练的停止头预测词元所需的迭代次数不足一半，但在标准停止规则下，词元实际上几乎每次迭代都会运行，因为这种训练方式从未对词元真正停止的那一次迭代进行评分。改为对每次迭代都进行评分可以解决这一问题，但在我们的实验中，只有在采用强烈偏向提前停止的惩罚时才有效。第二，计算节省量通常以每个词元的平均迭代次数来报告，但当序列以批次方式生成、且需运行到批次中最慢的词元停止为止时，没有停止头的模型在同等计算成本下表现几乎一样好。
tldr: 本文揭示循环语言模型中的停止头因训练方式缺陷和批次生成机制而无法真正节省计算量，无停止头的模型在同等计算成本下表现几乎一样好。
en_tdlr: This paper shows that halting heads in looped language models fail to genuinely save compute due to flawed training and batch generation dynamics, with head-free models performing nearly as well at the same computational cost.
